prize_parts.citation: For the invention of the optical lattice clock, based on magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, and for its development to a fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, opening a new regime of precision measurement.

statement.case_for: I move from dynamical mean-field theory (B001) to optical lattice clocks (B041). My reasons are specific. In round 1 I kept B001 because its conceptual originality and thirty years of confirmation seemed to me at least as strong as the experimental candidates, and I still hold that view of the science. But the chair's summary shows that no other member carries B001 as a configuration, and the one concrete problem I conceded myself, the omission of Metzner from a three-name limit, has not been answered by anything in the round. A citation that credits the infinite-dimension limit and the impurity mapping to a trio that leaves out one of the two originators of the limit is not one I can defend as a final public position, and I will not keep it merely to hold a place. B041 has the cleanest attribution on the table: Katori for the magic-wavelength concept and first lattice clocks, Ye for the systematic-uncertainty control and record accuracy. The achievement is mature, independently reproduced by several laboratories, and its accuracy rests on quantitatively understood physics (light shifts, blackbody, collisions) rather than on engineering alone. I already said in round 1 that I would not oppose it if the committee prizes unambiguous credit, and the exchange has strengthened that view. I keep B001 and B046 as my alternatives, B001 because I still think it is the strongest theory achievement on the list.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection, raised by Kroll and Eriksson, is that lattice clocks refine the line already honoured by the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, so a colleague outside atomic physics could read the prize as incremental. Its reach into new physics (varying constants, geodesy, tests of relativity) is largely prospective, and the second has not been redefined. Strontium, ytterbium and ion-clock groups elsewhere contributed to the accuracy record and fall outside a two-name credit. From my own standpoint it is also a precision-measurement achievement rather than a new conceptual framework, which is why it was not my first preference. Finally, I disclose that I am not an expert in atomic clocks and am relying on atomic-physics colleagues for the metrological detail.

responses.point: Eriksson moved from B001 to B046 but keeps B001 as first alternative, argues an open pairing mechanism is no reason to wait, and says the Metzner and Muller-Hartmann gap must be stated openly.
responses.response: We agree on the Metzner gap, and since you moved away from B001 yourself, I now accept that nobody is going to carry it this year with a three-name limit. On B046 I take your distinction seriously: a prize for the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated and superconducting phases does not require a solved pairing theory, and I concede that reproduction across several moire platforms is better than I weighted it in my opening. I do not move to B046 because my maturity concern is not only about the mechanism but about which phases and which experimental credit will survive; the Cao, Dean, Yacoby and Young contributions are exactly the part I cannot resolve within three names. I would not object to B046 later, and it is my second alternative.

responses.point: Kroll argues B041 has a clean two-person attribution, reproduction in several laboratories and 1e-18 accuracy, and he discloses his stay in John Hall's laboratory.
responses.response: I accept your attribution argument and it is the main reason I now carry B041. On your disclosure, I read it as a documented link to a mentor and not a collaboration with Katori or Ye, and I consider disclosure sufficient, though I would defer to the chair if colleagues disagree. I want to press one point from our round-1 exchange: my reservation about prospective reach still stands, since the redefinition of the second has not happened. But I have come round to Lindroth's view that the prize can rest on demonstrated, independently agreeing performance, and that a redefinition would follow from it and is not a precondition.

responses.point: Lindroth argues B041 is physics and not engineering because the 1e-18 figure exists only because light shifts were understood and suppressed, and says the comb provides the counting of optical cycles while the lattice clock provides the reference.
responses.response: That distinction between the comb and the lattice clock is the most useful answer anyone gave to the overlap worry, and it moved me. The citation should therefore be written around the magic-wavelength idea and the control of systematic shifts, and not around accuracy alone, so I have worded it that way. I also share your caution that the other strontium, ytterbium and ion-clock groups cannot be represented by two names; I think the committee should say so in the discussion and accept that cost, because it is smaller than the attribution problems on B001, B030 or B031.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B046 first as a theory prediction confirmed by decisive experiment, judges eight years since the discovery as timely, and doubts B030 counts as a discovery of a phenomenon with disputed priority.
responses.response: On B030 I agree and I have dropped it as a lead; the priority question among Evans, Cohen, Gallavotti, Searles, Jarzynski and Crooks is genuinely unresolved. On B046 I accept that the merit is not in dispute and that the theory-then-experiment pattern is clean. Where we still differ is timing: I would rather see a few more years in which the pairing mechanism and the stability of the correlated phases are tested before a prize, whereas B041 has an established record. If the committee decides that B046 is the principal proposal I will not treat that as unreasonable.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see lattice clocks as a distinct achievement or as incremental to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, a judgment on which colleagues in atomic physics are better placed than I am.
Whether recognition should wait for the formal redefinition of the second.
Whether a two-name credit can be defended given contributions from other strontium, ytterbium and ion-clock groups.
Whether I weigh B046 too cautiously on maturity, since several members argue that the discovery is secure irrespective of the pairing mechanism.
Priority details for the magic-wavelength concept and early lattice-clock demonstrations are from memory and not verified against the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B041 (Katori, Ye), B001, B046 or B030: none of my listed co-authors or institutions overlap with the credited names. I have disciplinary affinity with fluctuation theorems and with the statistical-physics foundations of DMFT, which is not a personal connection. I note Kroll's disclosed link to John Hall's laboratory and consider it disclosure rather than a reason for recusal. The roster does not state the terms of my co-opted service.
